source.title: Understanding the Generalization of Stochastic Gradient Adam in Learning Neural Networks
source.authors: Xuan Tang; Han Zhang; Yuan Cao; Difan Zou

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices and experimental results, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how batch size and weight decay affect train and test error using theoretical analysis and experiments, but does not reproduce the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: Theoretical results and reported experiments on batch size, Adam versus AdamW, and weight decay bear on V4 or V5. Figures 1, 2, 7–12 report results without recoverable precise values in the supplied text; figure-only rows preserve the authors’ textual descriptions. The feature-learning and noise-memorization measurements are not rows because the versions do not name those measurements.
record.test_reason: The study tests V5 through fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons reporting held-out error, supplemented by theoretical analysis. Adam–AdamW weight-decay sensitivity does not establish V4's generalization difference relative to SGD or recovery of that difference.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors attribute poor large-batch generalization to noise fitting and good mini-batch generalization to stochastic updates combined with suitable weight decay. They establish a narrower effective decay range for Adam than AdamW. These mechanisms are proved for a restricted two-layer synthetic image model; the deeper-network experiments corroborate performance trends.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes stochastic Adam and AdamW, including synthetic theory and image-classification experiments; it does not use random-label training or the original studies’ interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size and weight decay change reported test performance. The study also reports robustness checks across random seeds and momentum settings, and describes batch-size and weight-decay results on an ImageNet-1K subset.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam test error rises sharply above decay 0.05, whereas AdamW remains robust at decay 0.5; theoretical results also give Adam a smaller effective decay range.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam has a narrower effective weight-decay range than AdamW in the tested image-classification settings.

record.problems: The theoretical analysis uses a simplified two-layer CNN and synthetic feature-noise data; the authors note it is restricted to two-layer image models. Real-world CIFAR-10 and ImageNet results are primarily in figures, whose precise values are not recoverable from the supplied text. CIFAR-10 batch-size results report the best test performance over three learning rates for each batch size.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 7–12 provide additional error-bar and ImageNet subset results, but their plotted values are figure-only in the supplied text and their descriptions repeat the batch-size and weight-decay findings already represented in R1–R12. Figures 3–6 measure feature learning, noise memorization, or training-accuracy dynamics rather than measures named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No comparison of fitting fixed random labels with fitting natural labels and generalizing on held-out examples.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No SGD or momentum-SGD comparator, limited-versus-broader tuning comparison, recovery of an adaptive-versus-SGD gap, optimizer switching, or language benchmark.
No language-model experiments or interventions testing longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, normalization changes, or removal of the batch penalty through an adapted recipe.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or comparison of generalization measures.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining.

missing.what: Theoretical classification-error results: under the stated data and optimizer assumptions, large-batch Adam and AdamW attain zero training error but test error at least 1/2 − o(1), whereas their mini-batch counterparts attain zero training error and o(1) test error. Record these as theoretical results with their batch-size and decay conditions.

record.verdict_notes: Figures 7–12 are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. Figures 5–6 actually plot both training and test error, contrary to the record's characterization as training-accuracy dynamics. The ImageNet subset experiments use 90 fixed epochs and report the same batch-size degradation. No V4 verdict is warranted without the required SGD comparison.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label comparison testing memorization/generalization coexistence.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

No comparison with SGD or momentum SGD, no language benchmarks, and no comparison of limited versus broader tuning. Tests Adam versus AdamW weight-decay sensitivity, but not switching from Adam to SGD.

Tests batch size effects on CIFAR-10 and a synthetic image-data model, plus an ImageNet-1K subset. Does not test language models or compare adaptive training lengths, warmup, normalization changes, or matched small-batch accuracy within the same epoch budget.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-measure comparison.
